note: Source 1 is unusable for this genre for the same structural reason UK garage was: 'jungle artists' returns jungle paintings, Jungle Book dubbing artists and Jungle Press Editions. Sources 3 and 4 are worse than unusable — the SERP for 'jungle music artists' is dominated by Jungle the London soul duo (Josh Lloyd-Watson and Tom McFarland), and also_talk_about returned 'tom mcfarland' at 300/mo as if he were a junglist. The two consensus lists that are genuinely about the music (Clash's NewGen feature, the Grammy revival piece) both cover the 2020s revival and name almost no 1990s figures. Every founder below therefore comes from source 5, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle_music. That is the argument for source 5 stated twice now in two genres. Source 6, the catalogue, ranks A Guy Called Gerald, Nia Archives, Tim Reaper, SHERELLE, Om Unit, DJ Storm, Mantra, Mani Festo, DJ Marky and Machinedrum — the only source that shows who is playing jungle in 2026.

required_records.title: Valley of the Shadows
required_records.why: named in source 5's list of the records that defined the sound; the darkside benchmark the 1991-1993 section is built around

required_records.title: Incredible
required_records.why: source 5 names it as the record that took jungle to the charts, and General Levy is one of only four 1990s names the Grammy consensus piece carries; the 1994-1995 section is the whole point of the page and this is its chart moment

required_records.title: Inner City Life
required_records.why: Goldie is returned by the consensus piece, by the catalogue at 4 sets, and by source 5's sibling article, where Timeless is named as jungle's outward route; this is the record that made the argument that jungle could hold a song

required_records.title: We Are I.E.
required_records.why: source 5: 'The track We Are I.E. by Lennie De Ice is often credited as being the track that laid down the foundations for jungle.' It was named in the prose with no player anywhere on the page.

required_records.title: 28 Gun Bad Boy
required_records.why: returned by source 5 as a named track and by source 6 at 7 sets. Gerald was on the page and the record was not, so the bridge from Manchester acid house to London jungle had no sound.

required_records.title: Tim Reaper
required_records.why: returned by three sources. Named on the page with no player, so the revival section described a living scene the reader could not hear. A DJ, so the medium is a set rather than a record: an NTS mix from our own catalogue.

known_gaps.title: Burial — Leviticus, 1994
known_gaps.why: named by source 5 among the defining tracks. Both artist and title appear in the page text, but with no player, and 'Burial' on a jungle page reads as the dubstep producer unless a 1994 Philly Blunt record is playing next to it.

known_gaps.title: Darkage — DJ Solo
known_gaps.why: named by source 5, present in the prose, no embed. Lowest cost of the source 5 records: it is a scene-setting citation rather than a record the argument depends on.

known_gaps.title: 4am Kru; Samurai Breaks; Napes; Om Unit; Mani Festo; Mantra
known_gaps.why: returned by the Clash consensus feature or the catalogue and absent from the page. Not required — one source each — but recorded so the next pass does not re-litigate them. Om Unit, Mani Festo and Mantra are catalogue-only, which by FIGURES.md makes them differentiators rather than gaps: names we can write about that the competing guides cannot.

known_gaps.title: Renegade Snares — Omni Trio, 1993; Babylon — Splash, 1995
known_gaps.why: not a gap. Both are embedded on the page and neither was returned by any of the six sources, so they are recorded here to stop a later pass reading their absence from the required list as an error. They are the writer's judgement, which the algorithm does not overrule.

known_gaps.title: Corrections to this file, 6 September 2026
known_gaps.why: Two recorded gaps were false. 'Original Nuttah' was already embedded on the page, and Nia Archives already carried a Boiler Room set. Both were written down as missing players. A research note that overstates is the same failure as one that misses, so the corrections stay here rather than being deleted.
